description: Prometheus stole fire from the gods and gave it to humans, then endured an endless torture. A myth about progress, cunning, and the price of freedom.

hero.hook: A Titan steals fire from Olympus. Humans gain civilization. He gains an eagle and a chain.

blocks.text: **Prometheus** was a Titan, a god of the earlier generation. His name means the one who sees ahead. In Greek myth he shaped the first humans, protected them against **Zeus**, king of Olympus, and paid for that choice with a horrifying punishment.
By stealing fire for mortals, he gave humans technology and knowledge. His torture in the Caucasus became the symbol of genius that dares to defy power.

The story goes that Prometheus modeled the first humans out of clay and water. His brother [[Epimetheus]] acted too fast. Told to equip the animals, he gave everything away: claws, wings, fur, speed. When the human's turn came, nothing was left. People were born fragile and defenseless.

Prometheus decided to make up for it. At a sacrifice at [[Mecone]], he cut an ox into two shares. Under an ugly hide he hid the good meat. Under tempting fat he hid the bones. **Zeus** chose the handsome share. Ever since, humans eat the flesh and offer the bones to the gods.
To hide the fire, Prometheus used a [[Ferule]] stalk. Its pith burns very slowly, and Mediterranean shepherds really did carry it as a portable lighter.
Furious at being tricked, Zeus took fire away from humans. With no heat and no light, they fell back into an almost animal life.

sections.title: Humans born naked, and a Titan's trick

blocks.text: Prometheus slipped onto Olympus. Depending on the version, he stole a spark from the chariot of the Sun or from the forge of **Hephaestus**, god of blacksmiths. He hid it in his hollow stalk and carried it back to mortals.

blocks.caption: Prometheus brings fire to humankind, the founding act of technology

blocks.text: For the Greeks, fire was not only a flame. It stood for **technology** and **reason**, everything that lets people transform the world. Zeus struck back. Against humankind he would later send Pandora. Against Prometheus the punishment was direct.
In ancient medicine, the **liver** was seen as the seat of emotion and vitality. Zeus picked that organ to break the Titan's will.
The Titan was chained to a rock face in the **Caucasus**. Every day an eagle ate his liver. Every night the organ grew back. At dawn the torture started over, without end.

sections.title: The theft of fire and the punishment

blocks.text: For centuries Prometheus refused to give in. He knew a dangerous secret: which woman would bear a son stronger than Zeus. Despite the torture, he said nothing. He became the symbol of resistance to tyranny.

The hero **Heracles**, son of Zeus, finally reached the Caucasus. He shot the eagle down with one arrow and freed the prisoner. Zeus accepted the pardon: Prometheus at last revealed the secret about the nymph **Thetis**. That is how the king of the gods avoided his own fall.
To honor the oath that bound him to the rock, Prometheus wore a ring made from the iron of his chains and a chip of stone. He stayed “bound” to the mountain, and free.

In the 5th century BC, the tragic playwright [[Aeschylus]] staged *Prometheus Bound*. Later the myth fed the ideals of science and progress. Mary Shelley gave *Frankenstein* the subtitle “The Modern Prometheus”: creating life without wisdom can destroy as easily as it builds.

The philosopher [[Gaston Bachelard]] even spoke of a “Prometheus complex”, the urge to know more than your own teachers. Today artificial intelligence and genetics are often compared to a new fire: an immense power that nobody fully controls yet.
**Prometheus** handed humankind civilization by stealing fire, endured a torture that lasted ages, and was finally freed by **Heracles**. Progress has a price, and so does divine power.
